taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepted species concept. Historical Verbena combinations remain useful search aliases in sources.
look_here_first: LOOK AT A MATURE LEAF: larger prairie verbena often has a fernlike outline with deeply once- or twice-divided blades and many narrow secondary lobes. Then compare terminal flower clusters and watch mature spikes elongate in fruit. Do not identify by pink-purple flower color alone.

project_inclusion.range_basis: South-central Texas floristic voucher set explicitly records G. bipinnatifida in Uvalde, Medina, and Real counties; Williamson and Travis are also independently documented.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Exact county voucher evidence; no inferred counties.

best_field_traits: leaves deeply 1–2-pinnately dissected, often strongly feathery
spreading hairs with some glandular hairs
commonly 10–40 cm tall in Williamson material
morphology_keys.comparison_training: G. pumila is lower and more compact, with smaller broadly ovate leaves divided into fewer broader lobes and a very short dense spike that does not elongate much in fruit. G. bipinnatifida looks more finely cut and feathery.
morphology_keys.leaf_arrangement: Opposite and decussate on 4-angled stems; petiolate, larger leaves often broad triangular in overall outline.
morphology_keys.leaf_dissected: Deeply 1–2-pinnately divided; larger leaf blades usually longer, with conspicuous SECONDARY lobing into relatively narrow ultimate segments. The single best vegetative character vs G. pumila.
morphology_keys.flowering_structure: Dense terminal spike, flat-to-rounded in flower; spike rachis extends conspicuously as fruits mature, and individual flowers/bracts can become spaced.
morphology_keys.fruit: Four dry nutlets (mericarps); in regional specimens about 3–4 mm each, inside the persistent hairy 5-toothed calyx.
field_checks: Compare mature leaves at same scale, not small juvenile leaves.
Inspect older fruiting head for elongation and separated calyces.
Check single calyx/flower tube in profile for supporting measures.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Against G. pumila: larger feathery deeply 1–2-pinnately cut mature leaves (versus broad little leaves with fewer fan-shaped major lobes and sublobes); flowering spike often elongates substantially in fruit (versus fruiting axis staying compact). Corolla diameter ~8–12 mm vs 7–8 mm can overlap; avoid color as primary key.

cross_genus_lookalikes.difference: Both can show divided leaves; Glandularia bipinnatifida more typically has compact flower heads at anthesis and conspicuous 1–2-pinnate foliage, while V. halei has slender, often open spikes and lower leaves variably dissected.
Both may have lobed leaves; Gulf vervain usually has coarser, predominantly 3-lobed leaves and elongate spikes, not feathery twice-divided foliage and terminal clustered Glandularia flower heads.
